Terra Nova is a magical place where the land and sea compete for your attention, where the island boreal forest reveals its secrets as you hike a trail, and where you can experience an evening of theatre under the stars. Reservations will open for long term camping in Newman Sound on February 9, 2026 at 8:30 am NT. **These sites may only be booked by calling 1-877-737-3783.** Reservations will open for all other camping on February 11, 2026 at 8:30 am NT [Reserve your\\ \\ campsite](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) [![two smiling individuals sitting on a wooden deck wrapped in blankets](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/UPDATE-2022/terra-nova_camp_640x360.jpg?modified=00010101000000)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/camping) ### [Camp your way](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/camping) Nestled in an old growth forest with the Atlantic Ocean lapping the edges, Terra Nova offers some of the best camping in Newfoundland. [![two individuals hiking in a forest](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/UPDATE-2022/terra-nova_hike_640x360.jpg?modified=00010101000000)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/ran-hik) ### [Take a hike](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/ran-hik) Lace up your boots for 80 km of hiking trails to explore. [![a blue, starry sky with some silhouette trees ](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/UPDATE-2022/terra-nova_ciel-sky_640x360.jpg?modified=00010101000000)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/nature/ciel-sky) ### [Discover the dark side](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/nature/ciel-sky) Experience the night sky as Newfoundland’s earliest peoples did in this dark sky preserve. ## Most requested - [Moose hunting](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/nature/forets-forests) - [Fire safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/sec-saf/feu-fir) - [Camping reservations](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/reserve) - [oTENTiks](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/camping/oTENTiks) - [Important bulletins](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/info/bul) - [How to get here](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/visit/com-get) - [Red chairs](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/visit/chaises-chairs) - [Job opportunities](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/info/emp-job) - [Film, photography, and special event permits](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/info/perm) ## Visiting Terra Nova National Park ### [Activities and experiences](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ) Things to do, camping, hiking, paddling, tours and programs, fishing and visitor centre. ### [Plan your visit](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/visit) How to get here, hours of operation, passes and permits, and red chair locations. ### [Camping](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/camping) Frontcountry, backcountry, and oTENTiks. ### [Tours and programs](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/activ/interp_2) Guided walks, junior naturalist, evening programs, special days, school programs, and more. ### [Passes and permits](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/visit/tarifs-fees) Daily visitor fees, camping and program fees, and more. Free admission for youth. ### [Safety and guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/sec-saf) Weather conditions, emergency contacts, hiking tips, camping tips, and wildlife. ## About Terra Nova National Park ### [Nature and science](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/nature) Moose management, fire management, species at risk, dark sky preservation, and monitoring. ### [Stewardship and management](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/info) Park management, important bulletins, and contact information. | | ### Contact us Telephone: 709-533-2801 Email: [terranova@pc.gc.ca](mailto:terranova@pc.gc.ca) Media enquiries: [NEFUmedia-mediasUGET@pc.gc.ca](mailto:NEFUmedia-mediasUGET@pc.gc.ca) ### Hours of operation May 15 to October 11, 2026 [See more details](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nl/terranova/visit/heu-hou) ### \#TerraNovaNP - [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/TerraNovaNP) - [Twitter](http://www.x.com/ParksCanadaNL) - [YouTube](http://www.youtube.com/ParksCanadaAgency) - [Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/parks.canada) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nl/nl-signalhill-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220707)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/signalhill) ### [Signal Hill National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/signalhill) Signal Hill celebrates St. John’s rich communications and military history, amidst spectacular city and ocean views. Enjoy military and musical performances, stirring ceremonies, coastal hikes, dramatic fortifications, and the iconic Cabot Tower. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nl/nl-capespear-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220707)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/spear) ### [Cape Spear Lighthouse National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/spear) Atop a headland at North America’s easternmost point, Cape Spear Lighthouse overlooks a parade of drifting icebergs and waters teeming with whales and porpoises. Its restored interior offers a glimpse into 19th century lightkeeping along Newfoundland’s unforgiving coast. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nl/nl-castlehill-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220707)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/castlehill) ### [Castle Hill National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/castlehill) An impressive fort stands sentinel above a seaside town. Stone walls and cast iron cannons are testaments to a turbulent past. This is Castle Hill National Historic site—bastion to the struggle for a continent. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nl/nl-hawthornecottage-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220707)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/hawthorne) ### [Hawthorne Cottage National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/hawthorne) Hawthorne Cottage was the Newfoundland home of legendary Arctic explorer Captain Bob Bartlett. See exhibits and artefacts from his voyages while admiring the nearly 200-year-old cottage, a fine example of the picturesque architectural style in Newfoundland. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nl/nl-ryanpremises-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220707)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/ryan) ### [Ryan Premises National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nl/ryan) On Bonavista’s scenic harbour, knowledgeable interpreters, diverse exhibits and displays within the Ryan Premises’ restored buildings bring to life a 19th century Newfoundland fishing enterprise and tell the tale of Canada’s East Coast fisheries dating back 500 years. # Fire safety

## Terra Nova National Park

Do your part and stay informed on the current fire danger status and regulations. Your actions can help prevent human-caused wildfires.

### What is fire danger?

Fire danger tells us how easily a fire could start, how difficult a fire may be to control, and how long a fire might burn in a specific area.

The fire danger rating is updated daily at 2 pm at the campground kiosks, at the Visitor Centre, and on various signs throughout the park.

**Low:** Fires are unlikely. A fire will spread slowly, burn at a low intensity and is relatively easy to control for fire crews.

**Moderate:** Fires may spread along the surface of the ground with the occasional tree or clump of trees igniting. Ground crews can usually contain these fires.

**High:** **8 am to 8 pm fire ban.** Fires can ignite easily, spread quickly, and be challenging for fire fighters to control.

**Very high:** **24 hour fire ban.** Fires can ignite easily, spread vigorously, and be very difficult for fire fighters to control.

**Extreme:** **24 hour fire ban.** Fires will ignite easily, spread furiously, and burn with extreme intensity. Wildfires burning under these conditions are very difficult for firefighters to control.

### Fire bans

Fire bans are based on local fire hazards, current and forecasted weather conditions, the amount of moisture in vegetation, the regional wildfire situation and the availability of responders and equipment. Current and forecasted conditions are evaluated on a daily basis.

A fire ban is a legal restriction on certain types of fires to prevent human-caused wildfires. In a national park, burning illegally could result in a minimum fine of $200. More serious offences may result in fines up to $25,000.

### Permitted and prohibited items

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/ab/waterton/WET4/nature/feu-fire/Icons/Camp-BBQ-(1).png)Enclosed gas or propane stoves and barbecues

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire_safety_heater_520x520.png)Electric heaters

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire-safety-campfire-520x520.png)

Wood burning campfires in Parks Canada fire pits

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire-safety-deep-fry-520x520.png)

Deep fryers

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire-safety-propane-520x520.png)

Propane fireplaces and fire rings

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire-safety-unsure-520x520.png)

If you are unsure, please ask a Parks Canada staff member

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/ab/banff/WET4/nature/Conservation/feu-fire/Icons/Chimney-(1).png)

Wood, pellet, briquette or charcoal burning devices, including in cook shelters

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/ab/banff/WET4/nature/Conservation/feu-fire/Icons/Tiki-(1).png)

Torches

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire_safety_candle_520x520.png)

Candles

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire_safety_lantern_520x520.png)

Propane and gas lanterns

![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/nl/terranova/d-j/fire_safety_firework_520x520.png)

Fireworks

### How to safely enjoy a campfire

- Always check if there’s a fire ban
- You may only build a campfire in a designated fire pit when camping in a national park. Some campsites have individual fire pits; others have communal fire pits.
- Keep your fire small and under control. Never leave a fire unattended.
- Only use firewood purchased in the park. **It is illegal to collect and burn wood from the forest.**
- **Soak it, stir it, and soak it again!** Make sure your fire is completely out before you go to bed at night or leave your campsite.
- Campfires are not permitted at some backcountry camping locations. Ask a Parks Canada employee before setting out on your hike.
- Report fire or suspicious smoke to park staff or call 1-877-852-3100.
